subject: 8766D94FDC82E2B41C7E6A2CA0AE8C69
introduction: In 1904 and again in 1907 the Ottoman government sent commissions of inquiry to ‘Akká, where ‘Abdu’l-Bahá was a prisoner, on charges laid by members of His own family: that He was raising a banner, building a fortress on Carmel, gathering a following against the Sultan. The second commission lodged with the accusers, refused to hear Him, and left recommending exile or death; while it was at sea the Young Turk revolution began, and within a year the Sultan was deposed and the prisoners freed. These readings are ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s accounts. The Bible knows the scene well: Haman’s petition against a scattered people, the charge that Nehemiah was building a wall to make himself king, the accusations before Pilate and at Thessalonica, Daniel praying “as he did aforetime” once the decree was signed. Nicodemus and Proverbs state the rule of fair hearing that the commission broke, and the Magnificat and Psalm 146 speak of what became of the Sultan.
questions: List the charges in readings 7 and 10. Why do political accusations so often serve against religious minorities?
‘Abdu’l-Bahá refused both to meet the commission and to flee. What did each refusal express? Compare Daniel.
Reading 28 thanks the commission. What attitude to one’s accusers does that show, and is it sincere or ironic?
The Sultan fell while the commission was at sea. How should believers speak of such an event, and what should they avoid claiming?

outside.why: A commission arrived and went straight to the accusers. He that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him.
Nicodemus to the council: doth our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he doeth?
Slanderous charges carried to the Sultan. Haman to the king: there is a certain people scattered abroad; their laws are diverse from all people; neither keep they the king’s laws.
Interrogated each day at the government office. Ye shall be brought before kings and rulers; I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay.

A petition filled with lies: that He raised a banner, proclaimed a kingdom. The charge against Nehemiah was the same, and his answer: there are no such things done as thou sayest, but thou feignest them out of thine own heart.
We found this fellow perverting the nation, and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, saying that he himself is Christ a King.
Fabrications by the unfair. False witnesses did rise up; they laid to my charge things that I knew not.
The calumny that they had converted large numbers. These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also; and these all do contrary to the decrees of Caesar.
Cablegrams to stop the building on Carmel. The builders of the wall, every one with one of his hands wrought in the work, and with the other hand held a weapon.
Committees came time and again with restrictions and torments. In perils by mine own countrymen, in perils among false brethren.
A governor who expected an easy sum. Thou shalt take no gift: for the gift blindeth the wise, and perverteth the words of the righteous.
He paid them no heed and would not meet them. He answered him to never a word; insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly.
Daniel, when he knew that the writing was signed, went into his house, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
A boat was ready to carry Him to safety, and He stayed. The hireling seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth.
All believed His life and name would be effaced. Fret not thyself because of evildoers; for they shall soon be cut down like the grass.
They resolved to send Him to Fezzan. Our God is able to deliver us; but if not, be it known unto thee, O king.
The commission was on its way home when the Sultan fell. He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree.
Put not your trust in princes; his breath goeth forth, he returneth to his earth; in that very day his thoughts perish.

The Sultan is said to have exercised the utmost justice toward Him. Paul asked prayers for kings and for all that are in authority. How do you read reading 27 beside readings 6 and 21, which speak of the same ruler’s commission as tyrannical?
Gratitude to the commission, whose accusations amounted to praise. Ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good.

shortfall: Readings 3, 5, 6, 9, 12, 14, 18, 19, 22, 23, 25 and 26 narrate the same events in further detail.
